scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-02.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log shows 0 records, i.e. no tariff changes were logged in the queried period.

F-03.statement: Of disputed bills, 1240 had ESTIMATED reads and 1785 had ACTUAL reads (3025 total), per billing-db disputed_bills_by_read_type.

F-04.statement: Dispute ticket response times for 2440 tickets show a median of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days, within the 3.0-day SLA.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 grants Lakeside Water Utility the ability to request route priority changes, executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager.

F-07.statement: route-log.lagging_routes lists 14 routes with distinct completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), detailing the manual-read completion shortfall at route granularity.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is mainly a ticket-handling capacity/speed problem, so an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes bills will resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August caused systematically incorrect bills, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: The AMI nightly export of register reads (H-MDMS-BILL) began failing or delivering invalid data around August, pushing more accounts to estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL.statement: Manual meter-read completion by MeterWorks Field Services (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded since August, increasing estimate substitutions and incorrect bills.

H-LEGITIMATE-USAGE-SPIKE.statement: Bills issued since August are largely accurate and reflect genuine usage increases; the ticket surge reflects a customer-perception/communication gap rather than a billing defect.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Field reading has been understaffed by three readers since July, causing routes to run late and increasing estimated-bill substitution for affected customers.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — a measurable shortfall in manual meter-read completion during the dispute-surge period. It does not by itself show how many of these shortfalls turned into wrong bills or disputes.

Still shows field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, across 9200 manual-read accounts. It no longer supports treating the field-read shortfall as a confirmed partial driver of the 41% estimate-linked dispute share, since E-10 shows the 320 estimate-substituted accounts span 40 routes while E-09 shows only 14 routes are lagging, so the shortfall covers only a minority of routes feeding estimated bills.

A query of billing-db's tariff change log returned zero records, indicating no tariff changes were logged for the period checked; this rules out a tariff change as the source of altered bill amounts, but does not speak to any of the currently listed causal hypotheses (AMI delivery, field reads, rule changes, usage spikes, response speed).
Of 3025 total disputed bills, 1240 (41%) carried an ESTIMATED read and 1785 (59%) carried an ACTUAL read, meaning most disputed bills were not based on estimate substitution at all.

Still shows that of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 (41%) carried an ESTIMATED read and 1785 (59%) carried an ACTUAL read. It no longer supports attributing the 41% ESTIMATED-read dispute share to the Aug-Sep field-read completion shortfall as a confirmed mechanism, because E-10 shows the 320 estimate-substituted accounts span 40 routes while only 14 are evidenced as lagging (E-09), so most estimate-substituted accounts sit outside the evidenced lagging routes.

CRM dispute-ticket response times across 2440 tickets show a median of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA, indicating ticket-response handling is currently fast, not slow. This weakens the premise that ticket-response speed is the driver of the dispute surge, independent of whatever is causing the underlying wrong bills.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a reader staffing shortfall of three positions since July causes routes to run late, pushing affected accounts to estimated bills; this is an unverified stakeholder account of a mechanism, not a measured count of accounts or bills affected.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that there has been no tariff change this year is a stakeholder claim that agrees with the existing tool-derived finding (E-02: tariff_change_log returned 0 records). It adds no new decision-relevant information beyond corroborating an already-ruled-out factor.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly shows disputes roughly doubled from Jun-Jul baseline (610, 590) to Aug-Sep (1180, 1260), confirming the magnitude of the surge quantitatively but giving no information about its cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document (E-08) is a contract clause confirming that route priority (dispatch) changes may be requested by the utility but must be executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation, matching the already-recorded K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint; it bears on authority over the push_route_update protected action, not on any causal hypothesis about the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes gives route-level granularity (14 routes, each with a distinct completion value; sample route R-00 at 0.70) underlying the aggregate 0.88 Aug-Sep manual-read completion shortfall already in F-01/E-01. It confirms the shortfall is spread across multiple specific routes rather than being an aggregate artifact, but it carries no staffing or cause information and says nothing about the 59% of disputed bills with an ACTUAL read.

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) shows 320 accounts carried an estimated read last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes. Since route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) identifies only 14 routes as behind schedule, the estimated-read account footprint spans far more routes than the ones evidenced as lagging, so the field-read completion shortfall covers only a minority of the routes feeding estimated bills; the observation carries no read-type, tariff, import-status or bill-amount fields, so it does not speak to bill correctness or the 59% ACTUAL-read dispute cause.

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-config.validation_rule_changes (E-11) shows rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (coinciding with the Aug-Sep surge onset), changed the high-consumption check to compare the raw register value against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling applied; BV-09 (2026-03-02, label text) is an unrelated cosmetic change. This is the first direct evidence of a billing import validation rule change aligned in time with the dispute surge, giving a concrete candidate mechanism (possible unit-mismatch false-positive on high-consumption flags) for the previously unexplained 59% of disputed bills carrying an ACTUAL read.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What causes the 59% of disputed bills that carry an ACTUAL read — a billing import rule change (H-RULE-CHANGE) or a genuine usage spike (H-LEGITIMATE-USAGE-SPIKE) — since neither is yet evidenced?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation must include billing-config rule review and/or customer communication about usage increases, in addition to field-read remediation.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule-change log for Aug-Sep 2026 and compare against bill-amount deltas for ACTUAL-read disputed accounts.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Scope dispute triage to classify by read type and flag ACTUAL-read disputes separately rather than assuming a single fix resolves them.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution: E-11 shows rule BV-17's high-consumption check (raw register value vs 12-month m3 history, no unit scaling) deployed 2026-08-01, timing-aligned with the surge, supplying an evidenced candidate rule-change mechanism per H-RULE-CHANGE; whether it actually produced incorrect bill amounts still needs confirmation via DA-BILL (per VOB-R-2 / VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE).

U-AMI-DELIVERY-HEALTH-UNVERIFI.question: Is the MDMS AMI read export (H-MDMS-BILL) actually delivering valid data, given mdms-export access is currently pending (recovery_decision HOLD, ACCESS_PENDING)?
U-AMI-DELIVERY-HEALTH-UNVERIFI.decision_impact: If AMI delivery is also degraded it could contribute to disputed bills beyond the field-read mechanism; this cannot currently be confirmed or ruled out.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-HEALTH-UNVERIFI.resolution_path: Resume AMI-delivery verification once the vendor (Telemetrix) provisions mdms-export access.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-HEALTH-UNVERIFI.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI delivery health as unverified; do not rely on AMI-sourced reads as confirmed-correct in bill-accuracy analysis until access resolves.

U-ESTIMATE-BILLS-ACTUALLY-WRON.question: Were the estimate-substituted bills in the disputed set actually incorrect in amount, or just disputed despite being reasonable estimates?
U-ESTIMATE-BILLS-ACTUALLY-WRON.decision_impact: Determines whether fixing the field-read completion gap actually reduces billing errors or only reduces disputes without a correctness gain.
U-ESTIMATE-BILLS-ACTUALLY-WRON.resolution_path: Compare estimated bill amounts against subsequent actual-read true-up amounts for the same accounts.
U-ESTIMATE-BILLS-ACTUALLY-WRON.safe_placeholder: Report field-read remediation as a candidate partial fix pending bill-accuracy confirmation, not a guaranteed resolution.

A-ESTIMATED-READS-IMPLY-INCORR.statement: Disputed bills with an ESTIMATED read are assumed to be the ones actually billed incorrectly due to estimate substitution; E-03 only measures read-type composition of disputes, not bill correctness.

A-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTES-DIFFERE.statement: Disputed bills with an ACTUAL read are assumed to stem from a cause other than field-read shortfall (e.g. a billing rule change or genuine usage spike), inferred from the read-type split rather than directly evidenced.
